title: Boom Truck Crane Safety
summary: Boom trucks tip over or collapse when loads exceed the load chart or the machine is not set up right. This talk covers inspections, load limits, outriggers, and communication.
talking_points: Confirm the boom truck has been inspected and is certified for use, then do the required operational inspection before the shift.
Set outriggers and check that support blocking is firm and secure.
Always verify the weight of the load and rigging. Never lift more than the crane's capacity or go outside the manufacturer's load chart.
Only trained, authorized workers operate the crane or give hand signals.
Keep the operator and the signal person in clear view of each other or on headset. Never lift or swing a load over people, and never walk under a suspended load.
Check that wind speed is safe for the lift. Warn others when loads are moving or overhead.
site_hazards_to_check: Missing or expired inspection or certification for the boom truck
Outriggers not fully deployed or blocking on soft or uneven ground
Load or rigging weight unknown or over the load chart rating
Workers positioned under or in the swing path of a suspended load
High or gusting wind, or blocked line of sight between operator and signal person
discussion_questions: What does today's load weigh, and where does that fall on the load chart?
Who is giving signals, and how will you communicate if you lose sight of each other?
What is the wind speed limit for this lift, and who is checking it?
